races.name: Racing TV Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Harry's Halo
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who thrives on soft ground but faces 71 days absence and must overcome traffic issues from the back
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown most of his form over 6f on ground softer than good; close third in big field over 5f at Doncaster in sole run this term; enters calculations off same mark back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Surprised
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner improving for new connections but carries 3lb apprentice allowance and needs pace collapse to be effective
runners_data.comment: Won Beverley novice (7f) as 2yo; promising Catterick run latest; this stiff test can suit
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who has dropped to 6f for last two starts; gradually back to form this season for new stable, close third over C&D (good to soft) most recently; possibilities off same mark.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong course form but requires good pace and clear passage from rear of field
runners_data.comment: Twice been unlucky in big-field Thirsk handicaps this spring; enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped well and looked rather unlucky in two races at Thirsk in April; two attempts over this C&D (soft) comprise a second-place finish and success; likely player if bouncing back from below-par effort last time.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer stepping back up in trip after recent 5f success but faces 5lb penalty and positioning challenges
runners_data.comment: Reduced mark appeals on form as recent as last September but he's struggled since
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a run of duck eggs with 5f success at Carlisle (good) ten days ago and although back up 5lb he remains well treated on historical data, which includes 6f win off current mark (two years ago); respected.

runners_data.name: Rich Rhythm
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner better over 7f but drops back in distance and must overcome moderate course record
runners_data.comment: Always the danger he'll fluff the start; on his last winning mark but comes with risks
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown most of his handicap form over 7f, winning twice on AW; however, both 2026 efforts suggest this return to 6f is worth exploring; effective on turf and he's on a handy mark.

runners_data.name: Too Much
runners_data.note: Only genuine early leader in field which creates tactical advantage but carries fitness concerns after 49-day break
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner who can miss the break and/or pull hard; didn't offer much on comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Has done her winning on AW but ran well in last two turf attempts; however, brings a doubt over current form, having performed poorly in sole outing this year; upset in stalls and withdrawn last month (28-1 at the time).

runners_data.name: Baba Reza
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from wind surgery after 186-day absence with significant fitness questions
runners_data.spotlight: Has had wind surgery on two occasions, namely prior to reappearance success in 2024 (off 3lb higher) and prior to this 2026 seasonal debut; today may prove the time to catch him.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner better at 7f but offers pace angle in weak speed contest despite poor recent Catterick effort
runners_data.comment: Three-time course winner who returned to form at Ayr last week; on the shortlist
runners_data.spotlight: Has done most of her winning at 7f; ran respectably in last 6f attempt but was disappointing at Catterick (usually one of her favoured tracks) most recently and needs to rebound.

runners_data.name: Macedonian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with inconsistent recent form who must overcome positioning issues and moderate 2026 efforts
runners_data.comment: Just 1-15 and inconsistent but on a handy mark and the return to 7f is worth exploring
runners_data.spotlight: AW scorer for previous yard; inconsistent for current stable and has failed to show his form in two starts this term; well treated on best turf efforts but he's not particularly solid.

races.paceDynamic: Too Much will lead from the start with Coconut Bay the only other horse likely to race prominently early, creating a very soft pace scenario. The majority of this field are hold-up performers (Harry's Halo, Surprised, Stirrup Cup, Pop Star, Rich Rhythm, Baba Reza, Macedonian) who will settle behind the modest early gallop. With limited early pace pressure, the leaders will control the tempo until the final 2f when the field converges. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those that can position handy, as they avoid the inevitable traffic problems when seven hold-up horses try to make their move simultaneously.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Too Much breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from Coconut Bay
scenarios.body: Too Much dictates a steady tempo and kicks clear in the straight while the hold-up brigade get trapped behind horses. The lack of early pace allows the leader to conserve energy for a decisive strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Bay and Too Much engage in an early pace duel through the first half
scenarios.body: The increased tempo sets up perfectly for the closers as both leaders weaken in the final furlong. Hold-up horses get the strong pace they need to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Nightmare Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace creates a bunched field turning for home
scenarios.body: Multiple hold-up horses encounter interference and trouble in running as they all attempt to find racing room simultaneously. Those with clear runs or handy positions capitalise on others' misfortune.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise Move
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses breaks from character and races more prominently
scenarios.body: An unexpected front-running display catches the field off guard and the tactical switch proves inspired. The move creates better positioning away from the crowded pack behind.

watchPoints.text: Too Much breaks slowly or lacks early pace, as this would eliminate the only reliable front-runner and create chaos
Coconut Bay shows more early speed than expected and pressures Too Much, potentially compromising both prominent runners
Harry's Halo and Stirrup Cup both get trapped behind the same horses turning for home given their similar hold-up styles
The apprentice riders on Surprised, Stirrup Cup, and Baba Reza make positioning errors in the crucial final 2f
Pop Star and Rich Rhythm both attempt to come wide simultaneously in the straight, creating interference for others

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Capilano
runners_data.note: Prominent runner gets ideal setup with Connor Beasley able to control tempo unchallenged from the front
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded 72,000gns yearling; inexperience was evident when a rallying third at Newcastle, finishing ahead of Caeruleus; improvement on the cards.

runners_data.name: Light Of Dawn
runners_data.note: Expensive newcomer with unknown running style but strong pedigree faces tactical disadvantage on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Made 140,000gns as a yearling and 625,000euros at a breeze-up sale; half-sister to ten winners including some some smart sprinters, while the dam was a 5f 2yo Listed winner; of major interest for several standout reasons.

runners_data.name: Deputy Vice
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse set solid standard at Chester but faces pace disadvantage and soft going concerns
runners_data.comment: £145,000 breeze-up 2yo by Mehmas; one of yard's 2yos is 3-3, including in Lily Agnes here
runners_data.spotlight: £145,000 breeze-up 2yo; had a good draw at Chester (6f, good; 11-1) and held his own in what looked a useful novice race; that sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Caeruleus
runners_data.note: Hold-up style has 2-length deficit to overcome from Newcastle meeting with Capilano
runners_data.comment: 80,000gns yearling who's only just turned two; the market will be the best guide
runners_data.spotlight: 80,000gns yearling; had only just turned two when fourth at Newcastle 20 days ago; has 2l to find with Capilano but this son of Blue Point was getting the hang of things late on.

races.paceDynamic: Capilano will lead from the front with minimal early pressure in this small field, setting a controlled tempo that suits his prominent style. Light Of Dawn and Deputy Vice possess hold-up styles but lack early pace, while Caeruleus also sits back. The lack of early speed creates a tactical race where the leader can dictate terms. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent horses who can avoid traffic problems and control the tempo from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Capilano Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Capilano leads unchallenged and sets moderate fractions.
scenarios.body: The front-runner exploits the lack of early pace to build an unassailable advantage, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on soft going. Capilano's recent third at Newcastle behind these rivals understates his ability when allowed to dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If Deputy Vice or Light Of Dawn produce strong finishing kicks despite the tactical setup.
scenarios.body: The soft ground helps stamina-laden finishers as Capilano's early advantage gets pegged back in the final furlong. Deputy Vice's Chester third sets a solid standard for the hold-up brigade to exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Light Of Dawn Debut Impact
scenarios.trigger: If the expensive newcomer Light Of Dawn shows immediate class on debut.
scenarios.body: The Karl Burke-trained newcomer justifies her massive breeze-up price with natural ability that overcomes tactical disadvantage. Her pedigree suggests early speed that could surprise the market.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Caeruleus Improvement
scenarios.trigger: If Caeruleus builds significantly on his Newcastle fourth behind Capilano.
scenarios.body: The Blue Point colt bridges the 2-length gap from Newcastle through natural progression and better tactical positioning. His hold-up style finds late room as others tire.

watchPoints.text: Capilano breaking smartly and establishing clear early lead without pressure from the small field
Light Of Dawn showing any early pace that could disrupt Capilano's tactical advantage
Deputy Vice and Caeruleus getting squeezed for room in the small field down the home straight
The soft going impact on the finishing kicks of the hold-up horses
Connor Beasley's tempo management on Capilano through the middle furlongs

races.name: Carlisle Racecourse Supporting IJF Beneficiaries Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pearl
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to French 1,000 Guineas/French Oaks winner Avenir Certain; easy to back but showed clear promise with 1l third in novice event at York (1m, good) where she was the sole newcomer (belated debut) in a field of seven; this 4yo filly is the form pick and open to progress to boot.

runners_data.name: Stolen Kisses
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to Italian 1m Flat/2m jumps winner Cult Figure, half-sister to 1m1f winner Givemehoperosa (RPR 73); dam 1m-9.4f scorer (100); pedigree doesn't set the pulse racing; belated debut aged four.

runners_data.name: Midnight Serenade
runners_data.spotlight: Twilight Son half-sister to winners Earn Your Stripes (5f/6f; RPR 59) and Willy Il Coyote (Italian 6.7f-1m); dam 1m4f AW scorer (58); yard not associated with winning newcomers.

runners_data.name: Always Blue
runners_data.comment: Promising second on debut at Ripon but today's tough task may be beyond her
runners_data.spotlight: One of the main form contenders, having finished second at Ripon (1m2f) then just over 1l behind Pearl when 50-1 fifth at York (1m); however, unlikely to reverse placings with that filly, who has bigger potential.

runners_data.name: Foxy Night
runners_data.comment: Pedigree suggests longer trips might suit but yard in good form so worth a market check
runners_data.spotlight: Bred to stay at least 1m; belied her 50-1 odds with fourth of ten, best of the newcomers, in 7f AW contest at Kempton; a possible danger, provided she builds on that effort.

runners_data.name: Marhayb
runners_data.spotlight: Finished 2l fifth of ten in 7f AW event at Newcastle where she started second favourite behind a gelding in the same ownership; recorded an ordinary RPR but may well improve with the experience under her belt.

runners_data.name: Fair Isle Sioux
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo mare who has been absent for over two years since her sole start, namely keeping-on fifth of seven in Redcar contest (6f, soft); likely best watched.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Live Handicap

runners_data.name: Mereside Spark
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing signs of improvement, 9 days since last run keeps him fresh but needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Best effort over 5f (soft); below par lately; bled from the nose latest; others preferred.
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden; proved somewhat resurgent with fourth of six upped to 6f at Catterick (good to firm; bled from nose) most recently; may build on that effort.

runners_data.name: Realistic Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from in-form Jardine stable, 21-day break could sharpen him but consistency remains a major question
runners_data.comment: Most racing in sprints; not without hope into such a weak handicap down 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden whose lack of consistency has continued for new stable; likely best watched unless the market suggests a big run is expected.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in good recent form with Jason Hart aboard, threatening to break her maiden tag in this grade
runners_data.comment: Better efforts so far both over 6f; stuck on well when second at Ripon latest; player.
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who ran well at Ripon (good) and Catterick (good to firm) last month, taking her record in 6f handicaps to 322; threatening to win a race of this nature.

runners_data.name: The Cyprus Pearl
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making turf debut from all-weather, significant question marks over effectiveness on this surface
runners_data.comment: Huge prices and well beaten in two starts to date; expect more of the same
runners_data.spotlight: Turf/handicap debutante who is far from solid on her AW form; the new scenario needs to make a big difference.

runners_data.name: Auspicious
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in top current form, unraced on ground softer than good presents only minor concern given recent C&D second
runners_data.comment: Won at Redcar three weeks ago and just 3lb higher here; strong claims for in-form yard
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on ground softer than good; ran well (neck second) over C&D ten days ago when bidding to follow up his narrow success at Redcar; remains in top form.

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: Only genuine front-runner in the field, 21-day break and return to sprinting from longer trips could spark improvement
runners_data.comment: Didn't offer a lot on her Wetherby comeback for new yard three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who has weak claims on her 1m/7f efforts this term for new yard but, judged on pedigree, may improve for this return to sprinting (second attempt).

runners_data.name: Breeze Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from wind surgery after 36-day break, physical improvement could unlock dormant ability
runners_data.comment: Offered little thus far, including two sprint nurseries; tongue-tie added for reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Broadly regressive maiden whose chance depends on the effects of physical tweak (wind surgery since last run).

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Garden
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 89-day absence, poor AW form suggests turf switch essential for competitiveness
runners_data.spotlight: Has recorded RPRs in the 30s on Newcastle AW; change of venue/surface needs to prompt a good deal of improvement.

runners_data.name: Charcon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with predominantly all-weather form, 114-day layoff and poor turf record create significant doubts
runners_data.comment: Poor form so far and first-time visor needs to spark improvement back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Far from solid on form mostly shown on Newcastle AW; failed to beat a rival in seller in sole turf attempt (debut).

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing improvement in handicaps, recent good form suggests she can remain competitive despite inconsistent past
runners_data.comment: 66-1 winner at Newcastle in October; needs to back it up now returned to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form since racing in 6f handicaps, recording 66-1 win on AW last autumn then 33-1 second at Catterick (good) on reappearance; may well remain competitive.

runners_data.name: Independent Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with fading tendencies, two recent non-finishes and 51-day break indicate poor current condition
runners_data.comment: Unable to get competitive in any of her five handicaps and she's hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Has achieved little in terms of form and two duck eggs this season highlight her poor chance.

races.paceDynamic: Truly Special is the only natural front-runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a steady but manageable pace on the soft going. Breeze Star may track him early but lacks the speed to apply pressure, while the bulk of this field consists of hold-up horses who will rely on late runs. With minimal pace pressure up front, Truly Special can dictate terms before the large pack of hold-up runners tries to close from off the pace. This tactical setup strongly favors prominent runners who can track the leader and kick before the back-markers can organize their finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Truly Special gets soft fractions and stays the trip better than recent longer distance efforts suggest
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to control the race completely, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on testing ground. His return to sprinting from 7f/1m efforts could unlock the improvement needed to hold off late challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going and moderate early pace sets up perfectly for strong finishers with tactical speed
scenarios.body: Auspicious and Battenburg Belle time their runs to perfection, using class and recent form to overhaul the leader. The hold-up horses finally get the race shape they need with a steady pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Package Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If wind surgery transforms Breeze Star or stable confidence behind a lesser-fancied runner proves justified
scenarios.body: Breeze Star benefits dramatically from his recent wind operation and tracks the leader before finding extra gear, or Lanarra continues her upward trajectory from recent improved efforts. The pace scenario suits but an individual performance exceeds expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Truly Special stops quickly and the field comes to a crawl, creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace becomes terminal when the leader fades, turning this into a messy sprint where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalize. Form lines become irrelevant in a slowly-run tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Truly Special must be monitored for early pace pressure as any challenge to his lead could compromise his stamina reserves
Breeze Star's market movement will indicate stable confidence in wind surgery benefits after 36-day absence
Auspicious showing any reluctance to race on ground softer than his usual good conditions could undermine his strong recent form
Late money on Realistic Dream or Lanarra might suggest their trainers expect significant improvement from recent efforts
Battenburg Belle's position turning for home will be crucial as she needs clear passage to deploy her finishing kick effectively

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with proven Carlisle soft ground form but mounting losing run threatens confidence
runners_data.comment: C&D scorer; in decent nick, fourth at Musselburgh latest; 2lb out of handicap though
runners_data.spotlight: Losing run is mounting up and her three fourth placings this season reflect stagnation, rather than building towards a win; that said, she has won over C&D (soft) and returns here off a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose form has declined since good 2024 spell, headgear applied suggests connections concerned
runners_data.comment: Won two in a row at about 1m (good) last summer; soundly beaten on return from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Solid spell of form last term featured two wins and three second-place finishes; has gone rather off the boil since but a revival would give her good claims off current mark.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner but has regressed since autumn, new trainer bounce possible after 13-day break
runners_data.comment: Maiden; makes handicap debut; best efforts have been on AW; first run on fast ground
runners_data.spotlight: Has gone rather backwards since a good autumn effort on AW, disappointing favourite on handicap debut (7f) most recently; chance depends on the effects of new trip and first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with decent soft ground record but poor overall strike rate of 1-13
runners_data.comment: Consistent last season; made low-key return but might be boosted by new cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Record is only 1-13 and her form has dipped a touch in two outings this term; normally a consistent sort otherwise and, as per many times, has frame possibilities if back on song.

runners_data.name: Blufferonthebus
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up finisher with two Carlisle wins and good recent form, returns to favoured venue
runners_data.comment: Hinted at revival with Beverley sixth latest, finishing well; very much one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: In reasonably good form, having made the frame twice last month, third at Catterick latest; dual winner at Carlisle (soft/good to firm) and returns to this venue off a favourable mark; respected.

runners_data.name: Angela's Baar
runners_data.note: Maiden hold-up type who showed promise when stepped up to 1m last time but lacks winning experience
runners_data.comment: Below-par fifth at Wolverhampton in February; switch to h'caps needs to spark progress
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden who has failed to build on debut promise; however, made some late headway upped to 1m last time and there may yet be a bigger effort in her in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Emery Down
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with poor handicap record but improving for new yard after 19-day freshener
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but her best form has come on AW and others hold stronger claims
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 0-11 in handicaps since AW maiden win; however, steadily heading back in the right direction for new yard, fourth at Yarmouth (1m) most recently; possibilities off reduced mark.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tendency to fade in finish, eight consecutive defeats suggest major form concerns
runners_data.comment: Last of ten on her return at Ripon (1m) 26 days ago; hood is reached for now
runners_data.spotlight: Far from convincing on her handicap form since winning Ayr maiden in April 2025; best watched unless the betting suggests a turnaround is likely.

runners_data.name: Music Academy
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner making handicap debut, question marks over handling first-time fibresand
runners_data.comment: Big step forward with Kempton third last month; can do better still so needs considering
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who posted best effort when third at Kempton (AW) on penultimate start; may be capable of progress now handicapping, provided she takes to first-time headgear; shortlisted.

races.paceDynamic: Music Academy is the only confirmed front-runner and will likely get an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop, with the seven hold-up horses and one prominent runner (Positive Thoughts) sitting off the pace. This creates a tactical race where the pace-setter controls proceedings without early pressure, allowing the field to bunch up turning for home. With good-to-soft ground aiding stamina and most runners needing to come from behind, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a finishing kick, particularly those with proven soft ground form like Blufferonthebus and Epidavros.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Music Academy gets a soft lead and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows Music Academy to dictate terms and kick clear when the field challenges, while late closers find themselves with too much to do. Front-running tactics prove decisive on testing ground where stamina matters more than pure speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The pedestrian early gallop suits the patient tactics of the hold-up horses who can unleash superior finishing speed in the final two furlongs. Blufferonthebus and Epidavros use their proven Carlisle form to maximum effect.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts tracks Music Academy and pounces at the right moment
scenarios.body: The Quinn-trained filly uses her prominent style to position perfectly behind the leader before making a well-timed challenge that catches the hold-up horses napping. Her class advantage over this field becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Music Academy stops quickly and the race becomes a lottery
scenarios.body: The leader fails to see out the trip on soft ground, creating a messy finish where any of the hold-up horses could emerge from the pack. Form lines become less reliable in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rosemary May's market support as eight consecutive defeats and finishing fade pattern suggest major problems
Monitor if Positive Thoughts gets too keen tracking Music Academy as she needs to settle for new trainer tactics to work
Check Music Academy's early pace as any sign of keen going could compromise her stamina on testing ground
Watch for late market moves on Ravishing Beauty as headgear addition suggests stable expects improvement
Observe Epidavros in preliminaries as 22-day break and mounting losing streak may affect confidence levels

races.name: Follow Racing TV On X Handicap

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form, needs significant improvement despite 13-day freshening break
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Classic Encounter on 2025 York form, but not at best last few runs.
runners_data.spotlight: Gained most recent success off 3lb higher last July, enhancing his good record at Ripon; not in anything like the same form since; difficult to support with confidence.

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who struggles on turf, may race too freely again in this strong pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Triple AW winner who failed to get home, having raced too freely, over 1m2f in that sphere last time (still ran respectably); 0-12 on turf but was a good second off 6lb higher in last attempt; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER - key pace angle removed from race
runners_data.comment: Has a broadly progressive record on turf for current yard; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Record for current stable includes periods of progression at up to 8.5f; seemed to need the run at York on seasonal debut but she'll need to leave the bare form of that duck egg well behind.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good Carlisle record, 8-year-old may benefit from strong early pace
runners_data.comment: 3-39 overall, last winning in August 2024, and he's probably best watched first time out
runners_data.spotlight: Form at Carlisle features a success in 2024 and close second last June, both off much higher marks; a possible danger provided he takes a sufficient step forward from Beverley reappearance duck egg.

runners_data.name: Sound Janet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from wind surgery, 38 days off may have helped fitness issues
runners_data.comment: Expensive to follow for Roger Varian before sold for 25,000gns; market useful
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up a few times for previous yard; folded tamely and finished last on stable/seasonal debut but her subsequent wind surgery may prompt a better effort.

runners_data.name: Concert Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better on all-weather, 73 days off suggests fitness concerns on turf return
runners_data.comment: All five wins have come here and he's been in good heart here of late; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Does most of his racing at Newcastle (AW) where he has registered all five wins; generally consistent this year but seems to have a difficult task back on turf, being 8lb higher than last attempt.

runners_data.name: Skinny Malinka
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse absent 591 days, market will reveal stable confidence after hurdles experiment
runners_data.comment: 0-7 under rules but made the frame four times for Ed Bethell in 2024.
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since pulled up in December 2024 when making hurdles/stable debut; consistent six-race maiden on Flat for previous yard; market instructive.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Leading horse with course and distance win, progressive form gives edge despite stumbling last time
runners_data.comment: Easily made all Carlisle on Friday; 6lb higher today but still a leading candidate
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive since November, particularly on good ground this spring; gained most recent win over C&D; best to forgive latest effort (stumbled start, unable to adopt usual front-running tactics); remains of interest.

runners_data.name: Redarna
runners_data.note: Hold-up 12-year-old veteran with Carlisle wins, drop in grade may revive aging legs
runners_data.comment: Nine-time course winner but he's struggled at Musselburgh and Thirsk this year
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who has been a prolific winner down the years, including at Carlisle; not solid on 2026 form but this drop back in grade may have positive effect; successful in last Class 5 attempt.

runners_data.name: Pink Azalea
runners_data.note: Front-runner with excellent Carlisle record, needs to rediscover early 2024 progressive form
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo filly whose handicap record is split into two halves, namely a progressive one followed by a dismal one; however, 1-1 at this track and could revive if her favoured soft ground materialises.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with poor course and distance form, 3lb claiming apprentice takes pressure off
runners_data.comment: Poor strike-rate but may have needed reappearance run and he's on a competitive mark
runners_data.spotlight: Made the frame in most starts last term for new yard but form has dipped in two outings this term, latest over C&D; doesn't look as if he's about to belatedly add to his Irish 2yo win.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good form stepping down in trip, may lack tactical pace for this distance
runners_data.comment: Having a good year and chasing a quick hat-trick; stamina for 1m4f still to be proven
runners_data.spotlight: Generally progressive on AW/turf this year, winning four times over 1m2f; creditable third over 1m4f at Musselburgh last time; remains in form and may still have more to offer at this level; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid recent form, proven soft ground performer gives major edge here
runners_data.comment: E-w player if in same form as 12 months ago (won this race); this time it's after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Has a record of 3-7 (Flat/hurdles) for current yard; creditable third at Newbury (1m4f, good) on seasonal debut most recently; major player off same mark, assuming he copes with this drop back in trip (stiff track and forecast slow ground are helpful in that respect).

runners_data.name: Titainium
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 322 days off, previous soft ground struggles are concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since a dismal effort on soft ground last July and again has a doubt over the forecast surface; has gained both turf wins on good to firm.

races.paceDynamic: Style Of Life (non-runner), Krissy and Pink Azalea will force a strong gallop from the start, with King Of Fury and Amancio likely to sit just behind this leading trio. The sustained pace over 1m1f on testing ground will stretch the field and expose any stamina limitations, particularly as the leaders try to maintain their positions up Carlisle's testing climb. The combination of genuine pace pressure and soft conditions will set up a scenario where horses need both tactical speed and staying power to be competitive. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina who can close late when the early pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed leaders go too hard early and crack in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will stretch the field but ultimately backfire on the pace-setters as they tie up on the testing ground. Late-closing hold-up horses with stamina will sweep past the faltering leaders in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Sustains Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy or Pink Azalea can maintain their gallop and see out the trip strongly
scenarios.body: The early leaders will set a searching pace but one of them has the class and fitness to sustain their effort all the way to the line. Prominent racers who can travel well within themselves will be best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the non-runner Style Of Life creates a more moderate early pace than expected
scenarios.body: With one key pace-setter removed, the gallop becomes more stop-start and tactical, suiting horses who can quicken rather than grind. Mid-division horses with tactical pace will benefit from the change in race dynamics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ground Deteriorates Further
scenarios.trigger: If the going becomes genuinely heavy and stamina becomes the sole determining factor
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of stamina where only horses with proven soft ground form and staying power can cope. Pace becomes irrelevant as the surface dominates tactics completely.

runners_data.name: Tarlac

runners_data.comment: Sole win came over C&D but not obviously in good enough form to capitalise on falling mark
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned mostly over 6f; inconsistent since sole win; his chance of taking advantage of a reduced mark partly depends on the effects of this return to 7f; record over this trip isn't fully conclusive.

runners_data.name: Pallas Lord
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner whose turf form is poor but gets tactical advantage as sole pace-setter, wearing tongue-tie for Donald Whillans
runners_data.comment: 1-1 here and a close third at Hamilton last time, but fast ground probably not ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Has recorded the majority of his wins on Newcastle AW; below par over C&D ten days ago, failing to build on his Hamilton effort; still hasn't scored on turf since 2022.

runners_data.name: Orbital Chime
runners_data.note: Hold-up type recently sold cheaply and showing declining form, visor applied but trainer James Owen in good touch this fortnight
runners_data.comment: Couple of expensive defeats lately; capable off this mark but strike-rate doesn't inspire
runners_data.spotlight: Poor strike-rate; eventually lost his form during spring spell with James Owen and was sold for 2,200gns since last run; best watched unless the market suggests a revival is likely.

runners_data.name: Jkr Cobbler
runners_data.note: Closer who has shown course form in the past but disappointed last time, returns to more suitable trip for in-form Andrew Mullen
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner who hasn't been running badly this year without the breaks; on handy mark
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained most wins at Ayr/Newcastle but he defied a higher mark over C&D two years ago; basically running okay this year until never dangerous last time; has the ability to take a serious hand.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse running 10lb below last winning mark with solid reappearance effort at Catterick, winless for current stable but well-handicapped
runners_data.comment: 5-40; ended last season on a downbeat note and no win since October 2023; monitor only.
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 0-13 for current stable but he remains 10lb below last winning mark and holds a good chance provided he builds on Catterick reappearance effort (finished third).

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Held-up runner who has struggled for new trainer Nigel Tinkler but defied higher mark over course previously, back quickly after latest effort
runners_data.comment: Sole success came over C&D from 4lb higher last August, but regressive since

runners_data.name: Albeyours

runners_data.name: Dolly's Delight
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose sole win came on fast ground, tongue-tie applied but brings concerns about handling the prevailing soft surface
runners_data.comment: Some work to do with Saisons d'Or from Southwell (fifth); the task isn't impossible.
runners_data.spotlight: Registered sole success on fast ground; has rather inconsistent form for current yard; brings doubts over the forecast surface and whether she'll be in top form.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent efforts suggest 7f may now be minimum trip, limited exposure at this distance but carries bottom weight
runners_data.comment: Of interest on 2025 best; should be at concert pitch after two runs back

races.paceDynamic: Pallas Lord is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the gates, likely getting an uncontested lead on the rail. With Tarlac and Dolly's Delight showing prominent tendencies but no aggressive pace-pressing history, Pallas Lord should be allowed to bowl along at a comfortable rhythm through the early furlongs. The bulk of this field comprises hold-up horses (Rwenearlytheredad, Orbital Chime, Jkr Cobbler, Ideal Guest, Sir David, Albeyours, Baby Rover) who will be content to settle and come from off the pace. This tactical setup strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will emerge when seven hold-up horses try to find racing room simultaneously in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord maintains a steady gallop without serious early pressure from Tarlac or Dolly's Delight
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old gets first run on his rivals and proves difficult to peg back despite his recent poor turf record. Seven hold-up horses get bottled up behind the pace and struggle to find clear runs when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes unsustainably fast or Pallas Lord weakens significantly in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of the closers pay dividends as they sweep past a spent leader with superior finishing kicks. Rwenearlytheredad and Ideal Guest benefit most from their class and proven course form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tarlac or Dolly's Delight track the leader closely and time their challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners avoids both the pressure of making the pace and the traffic problems faced by the hold-up brigade. They get first run on the leaders while having enough left to resist the late closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord stops dramatically and the prominent horses also fail to deliver their finishing kicks
scenarios.body: The race falls apart tactically with weak early fractions followed by no sustained pressure, allowing a hold-up horse with the strongest finish to emerge from the pack. This chaotic scenario suits horses with proven acceleration despite poor positioning.
